gaps.gap_id: B1 — contract_balances has no block_number; destructive per-contract DELETE + re-insert
gaps.real: YES, and worse than stated. Query: `select count(*), count(distinct cb.fetched_at), max(fetched_at)-min(fetched_at) from contract_balances cb join contracts c on c.id=cb.contract_id where c.protocol_id=1` -> 721 rows / 26 distinct instants / span 01:40:25.469544. `\d contract_balances` -> id, contract_id, token_address, token_name, token_symbol, decimals, raw_balance, usd_value, price_usd, fetched_at. NO block_number AND NO observed_address. The DELETE is services/monitoring/tvl.py:236 (gap text said :235) and a SECOND writer does the same at workers/resolution_worker.py:382. (a) The quoted ETHFI figure only PARTLY reproduces: ETHFI carries 4 distinct price_usd values; 0.40097100@20:05:02 -> 0.39764700@20:37:20 is +0.836% but over 32.3 min, not 23; the ~23-min pair (0.39764700@20:37:20 -> 0.39600200@20:59:59) moved 0.414%. A third axis the gap does not mention: prices diverge WITHIN one fetched_at — ETHFI 0.39764700 (5 rows) vs 0.39613400 (1 row) at the identical instant 20:37:20.659608 (0.382%), liquidETH 2047.91 vs 2477.38 at that same instant (20.97%). No block column can fix intra-instant price divergence; it is a separate provenance axis. (b) Quantified non-replayability: I re-read all 571 ethereum (runtime-address, asset) ERC-20 pairs via Multicall3 at pinned block 25643300 — 571/571 sub-calls succeeded, 481 match the stored raw_balance byte-for-byte, 90 (15.8%) differ. On the #2 value row: EtherFiRestaker stETH stored 248064483601702256055347; balanceOf at 25641090 (the fetch-minute block) = 248064483601702256055348 (+1 wei); at 25643300 = 267464483601702256055348 = +19,400.000000000000000001 stETH ~ +$36.5M (+7.82%). This reconciles B0b's '267,464.48 stETH' with the stored 248,064.48 — both right, at different heights, and nothing in the table says which. (c) ENTITY-KEY defect (ledger L-118, independently reproduced and quantified): 16 of the 60 balance-carrying protocol-1 contract rows are IMPLEMENTATIONS of a protocol-1 proxy, and 13 of those 16 proxies carry zero balance rows. The money is the proxy's: LiquidityPool impl 0x17a16747 reads 0 wei at 25641090 / 25643300 / 25644042 (codelen 45216, a live contract) while proxy 0x308861a4 holds 41152427567680411972276 wei at 25641090 vs the stored 41151736179074411972276 (0.0017% drift). Same shape for stETH@0x51357a70 (0) vs @0x1b7a4c37 (exact match) and eETH@0xa6ca0607 (0) vs @0xcd5fe23c (exact match). 88.7% of the protocol's $4.16B sits on impl-keyed rows. Mechanism is one line: workers/resolution_worker.py:342 `target_address = request.get("proxy_address") or address` — read at target_address, written to contract_row.id (:411, :426). Writer split confirmed by a fetched_at-multiplicity partition: the single instant 20:37:20.659608 is one tvl.py cycle (35 contracts / 446 rows, 0 impls — tvl.py:105-122 correctly excludes impls); the other 25 solo instants are resolution_worker writes and carry ALL 16 impl-keyed sets. 18 of 60 entities were fetched at an address different from contracts.address; 16 repairable via contracts.implementation, 2 NOT (see flips_existing_rows). (d) Double-count: 5 proxy/impl pairs, 20 overlapping (pair, asset) rows with byte-identical raw_balance, min-side sum $1,589,342.37 — FIELDS.md's dollar figure reproduces to the cent, but its 'measured: 2 pairs' undercounts (3 of the 5 pairs are $0.00). The duplicated rows carry DIFFERENT usd_value for identical raw_balance (778407.77 vs 781662.77 = 0.418%).
gaps.fixable: Schema: db/models.py:1269 (class ContractBalance). Writer 1: services/monitoring/tvl.py:236 (delete), :239-256 (native insert), :258-270 (ERC-20 insert). Writer 2: workers/resolution_worker.py:382 (delete), :388-419 (native), :421-434 (ERC-20). IS THE BLOCK IN SCOPE THERE? NO. utils/etherscan.py:538 `get_eth_balance` sends Etherscan `account/balance` with tag="latest" and returns only data["result"]; utils/etherscan.py:639-646 `get_token_balances` calls `addresstokenbalance` with page/offset and NO block parameter at all, and neither response carries a height. The address actually read IS in scope (tvl.py:178 `address = contract.address`; resolution_worker.py:342 `target_address`), so observed_address is writable today at both sites with zero new evidence.

gaps.honest_publication: For all 1,617 existing rows (721 protocol-1): as_of_block = not_determined, PERMANENTLY — nothing stored recovers the height, and fetched_at is a write timestamp, not an observation height. observed_address = not_determined per row (recoverable only by re-deriving jobs.request->>'proxy_address' via contracts.job_id and checking against chain — a re-derivation, not a stored witness). gaps.gap_id: B2 — absent native row conflates proven-zero with fetch-failure
gaps.real: YES as a code fact; 0-REALIZED as damage on this corpus. Population: 41 of 60 protocol-1 balance-carrying entities have NO native row, 19 do (19 native / 702 ERC-20 / 721 total) — the gap's figure reproduces exactly. Code: services/monitoring/tvl.py:239 `if eth_wei > 0:` gates the insert; tvl.py:223-227 is the swallow (`except Exception as exc: logger.warning(...); eth_wei = 0`) — the gap text's ':224-227' is off by one at the start and ':238' by one at the gate. THE SECOND SITE (garbled as '...tion_worker.py:387') is workers/resolution_worker.py:388, and the two writers behave DIFFERENTLY: resolution_worker.py:357-377 returns EARLY on a native-fetch exception, BEFORE the DELETE at :382, leaving prior rows intact and recording record_degraded(phase='balance_fetch') — fail-closed. tvl.py has NO record_degraded on this path, only a logger.warning, so a tvl.py native failure leaves ZERO persisted trace. Third, both writers swallow the ERC-20 side identically: utils/etherscan.py:647-656 catches RuntimeError, records degraded, and `return []`, so tokens_raw is never an exception for the common Etherscan error and the worker proceeds to DELETE and write an empty token set — the docstring at :648-650 says so verbatim. Persisted evidence in this run: folding all stage_errors artifacts gives 1,839 entries, 44 with phase='token_balance_fetch' (all 'Etherscan error: No token found - []') and ZERO with phase='balance_fetch'. CHAIN-CORRECT ON-CHAIN CHECK (I got this wrong once and corrected it — see could_not_verify): protocol-1 contracts span two chains (ethereum 42 entities, optimism 18), so each must be read on its own chain. At ethereum block 25643300 (ts 2026-07-30T04:32:47Z) and the time-aligned optimism block 154893595 (same timestamp, found by binary search on block timestamps): of the 41 entities with NO native row, 0 have a nonzero native balance (26 ethereum + 15 optimism, all zero). So the conflation is ARMED and currently 0-realized — no published fact is wrong today because of it. Separately, 6 of the 16 ethereum entities that DO have a native row read 0 wei at the pinned block: 5 are B1's impl-keyed rows (LiquidityPool, WithdrawRequestNFT, MembershipManager, EtherFiNodesManager, CumulativeMerkleDrop) and the 6th is AuctionManager, whose money sits at its jobs.request proxy_address.
gaps.fixable: services/monitoring/tvl.py:239 and workers/resolution_worker.py:388 — both the exact `if eth_wei > 0` gate, and at both points the three states ARE distinguishable in scope: tvl.py:225 knows it is in the exception handler; resolution_worker.py:352-357 holds eth_wei_raw and can test isinstance(..., BaseException); and eth_wei == 0 after a successful call is a distinct known state. The fix is 'always insert, with a status discriminator' and the discriminator is already computable — nothing new must be learned.
gaps.provable: PROVABLE for the zero via deterministic on-chain read (pinned block): eth_getBalance(addr, hex(block)) returning 0x0 IS a proven zero for that address at that height (exercised on 60 addresses across two chains at time-aligned pinned blocks). NOT PROVABLE from the current Etherscan account/balance?tag=latest path, whose answer carries no height — a zero from it is 'zero at some unrecorded moment in a 1h40m window'. And explicitly NOT PROVABLE by the rejected route: treating an absent row as $0 is the reject-list item, and reading eth_wei = 0 after the swallow as a zero is the same error one layer down — which is precisely what tvl.py:227 does today. The FAILURE state is provable trivially (the exception object is in hand); what is not provable is any claim about the balance on that branch.
gaps.proposed_witness: Insert unconditionally, with `native_status varchar` in {proven_zero, proven_nonzero, fetch_failed} plus B1's block_number and observed_address. proven_zero may be written ONLY on the pinned-RPC path (a zero from the unpinned Etherscan path is not_determined — carried by NULL block_number or a fourth value). Emit record_degraded on tvl.py's native path too, so both writers leave the same persisted trace. Apply the identical treatment to the ERC-20 empty list: `asset_set_status` in {returned_assets, returned_empty, fetch_failed, at_page_cap}, since `return []` at utils/etherscan.py:656 makes 'fetch failed' and 'holds nothing' the same row-set.
gaps.honest_publication: For the 41 rows with no native row: per-asset native value = not_determined, never $0, and never 'the contract is unfunded'. scoring_prototype/score_v3.json already publishes this correctly at value_provenance.absent_native_row, and B0b/R5's decisive rule stands — the sweepETH/withdrawEther floor is licensed by the destination proof, not by the balance snapshot. Additionally publish 'no persisted discriminator exists for the tvl.py-written rows': the writer identity itself is recoverable only by a fetched_at-multiplicity heuristic (one shared instant = a tvl.py cycle), not from a column.

gaps.gap_id: B3 — fork verdicts span 51 distinct blocks in one run
gaps.real: YES, and the register misfiles WHERE the field lives. `select count(*), count(witness->>'block_number') from effect_verdicts` -> 274 rows, 0 with a block_number: effect_verdicts.witness has NO block key (its 20 keys are observation, reason, value_moved, shape_proved_by, destination_shape, observed_blast_radius, scored_denominator, pre_pause_succeeding, pause_effective, input_seeded, revert_reason, supply_delta_sign, backing, latch_flip, duration_bound_seconds, timelock_executed, duration_bound_source, witness_asset_held, auto_expiry, contract_balance_seeded). FIELDS.md §7's row 'effect_verdicts.witness.block_number | 304/304' is WRONG on both location and denominator (274 verdict rows exist). The block lives only in the transcript blobs: I folded all 304 effect_transcript_* artifacts from MinIO — 304/304 carry block_number, 51 distinct values, min 25640764, max 25641259, SPAN 495 blocks (~99 min at 12s). The 51 reproduces exactly. Finer than the gap text: 47 jobs produced them and 7 jobs carry TWO different blocks each (deltas 21-50), and in every one of the 7 the tier1 and tier2 transcripts draw from the SAME two-value set — so the pin is per effects-stage INVOCATION, not per job. WHERE the height is chosen: workers/effects_worker.py:684-717 `_preflight` — one seams.block_number() per invocation, block = 0 on failure, and supported = False if a supported simulate cannot be pinned (fail-closed, correct). Carried as ProbeContext.block (services/effects/orchestrator.py:71, :88) into SimContext and recorded by services/effects/harness.py:204. NOT in services/effects/anvil.py or simulate.py as the gap text guessed. A SEPARATE, sharper defect: services/effects/anvil.py:667-683 `_build_anvil_cmd` passes --fork-url with NO --fork-block-number, and production does fork (workers/effects_worker.py:537-540 SubprocessAnvil(fork_url=rpc_url)), so a tier-2 anvil fork is taken at the upstream's latest head at spawn while anvil.py:176-183 / :430-437 rebuild SimContext with the preflight's ctx.block and new_transcript records THAT. For the 78 tier2 transcripts (including all 4 proven freeze verdicts) the recorded block is provably not the observation height, and the real height is recorded nowhere — the tier2 key set is exactly [anvil_version, auto_expiry, block_number, calls, chain_id, contract_address, delay_seconds, duration_bound_source, effect_class, feature, fixtures, foundry_version, hardfork, max_pause_duration, observed_blast_radius, pause_effective, pre_pause_succeeding, predicted_guard_set, results, tier, version].
gaps.fixable: Two independent fixes, both in scope. (a) Publish the height on the verdict: witness is jsonb, so NO migration — the block is in scope as the transcript's own field (services/effects/harness.py:204 puts ctx.block into tr; db/effect_cache.py:951-1002 record_effect_verdict receives witness; recipes already merge transcript-derived keys into it, e.g. services/effects/anvil.py:363-371). (b) Make the recorded height true for tier 2: pass --fork-block-number str(ctx.block) at services/effects/anvil.py:676 — the block is available to the caller building the transport (workers/effects_worker.py:507-541). (c) One block per RUN needs a run-scoped identity all of a protocol's jobs share; jobs has protocol_id but no run/batch column, so a per-run pin is a NEW schema decision, not a refactor.
gaps.provable: PROVABLE — a deterministic on-chain read (pinned block) whose height is already a local integer at the write point; publishing it invents nothing. The tier-2 fork-height fix is a name-free plumbing change (an explicit CLI argument replacing an implicit 'latest'). NOT provable: any retroactive claim about the 78 tier2 rows' true height — --fork-block-number was never passed, so it is unrecoverable and must be published as not_determined.
gaps.proposed_witness: witness.block_number (the height the fork was taken at — from --fork-block-number for tier 2, the preflight pin for tier 1) plus witness.block_source in {run_pin, job_pin, invocation_pin} so a consumer can tell a run-scoped pin from today's per-invocation one. The verdict identity should include the block: uq_effect_verdicts_identity is (chain_id, contract_address, selector, effect_class) with no height, so a re-analysis silently overwrites an observation taken at a different world state.
gaps.honest_publication: WHICH OPTION PRESERVES inv.12: neither alone. Pinning one block per run makes the run internally coherent (today a contract's value verdict and its freeze verdict can be 50 blocks apart within ONE job) but does not make re-analysis a no-op, because the next run pins a new head. Publishing the per-verdict block AS PART OF THE WITNESS IDENTITY is the one that satisfies inv.11 (the block becomes a persisted input) and lets a consumer separate 'changed because the height changed' from 'changed because the world changed' — the only form inv.12 can take for a fork observation. So: publish the block as identity (necessary) and additionally pin per run (desirable, for intra-run coherence). Until then all 274 verdicts must read 'observed at an unrecorded height within a 495-block window', and the 78 tier2 rows must read 'height not_determined' rather than carrying the preflight block as if it were the fork height.
gaps.deterministic_test: tests/test_effects_block_identity.py, no wire. (1) drive the orchestrator with a stub block_number seam returning 25643300 and a stub anvil transport; assert the emitted verdict's witness carries block_number=25643300 and block_source='invocation_pin', byte-exact. (2) assert _build_anvil_cmd(bin, port, 'prague', 'http://u', None) == ['anvil','--port','...','--hardfork','prague','--silent','--fork-url','http://u','--fork-block-number','25643300'] — an exact list compare, so a future edit dropping the pin fails. (3) FAIL-CLOSED: stub the block seam to raise; assert simulate_supported is False, NO tier-1 transcript is emitted, and any tier-2 verdict carries block_number=None with block_source absent (never 0 — today block = 0 is the sentinel and 0 would read as genesis). (4) DETERMINISM: run the same stubbed probe twice at the same pinned block and diff the two verdict rows byte-for-byte, in the style of scripts/determinism_gate.sh.
gaps.cost: No migration for (a) — witness is jsonb. (b) is one CLI argument. Extra RPC: zero for (a); for (b), pinning anvil to a fixed height rather than latest may increase lazy state fetches if the height is colder than the upstream's cache (unmeasured). A per-run pin needs a new jobs column. Does not rewrite existing rows; the 274 existing verdicts gain nothing and stay not_determined, so the value is forward-looking. No re-analysis needed to land it; one is needed to benefit.
gaps.flips_existing_rows: No verdict value changes. It changes the PROVENANCE meaning of 78 rows — the tier2 verdicts whose recorded block is not their observation height — including the four proven freeze verdicts effect_verdicts.id 137 (0x1b7a4c3797236a1c37f8741c0be35c2c72736fff), 149 (0x308861a430be4cce5502d0a12724771fc6daf216), 173 (0x35fa164735182de50811e8e2e824cfb9b6118ac2), 219 (0xcd5fe23c85820f7b72d0926fc9b05b43e359b7ee), all selector 0x7e3db158. score_v3.json's replayability.non_replayable_inputs[1] would need to become 'plus 78 rows whose recorded block is not the fork height'.
gaps.small_populations: The 7 two-block jobs and the 4 proven freeze verdicts inside the 78 tier2 rows. Neither may calibrate a rule (B14); they are named as instances, and the fix is argued from the code contract (an unpassed --fork-block-number) rather than from their count.

gaps.gap_id: B4 — observed_reach_floor_usd and its siblings produced on 0 rows
gaps.real: PARTLY — the zero is real, the '7 sibling observed keys' framing is wrong. Measuring every projected `observed` key over protocol-1 claims gives exactly EIGHT keys at population 0, and only FOUR are in the reach family: observed_reach_floor_usd 0, observed_reach_rejected_usd 0, protocol_tvl_usd 0, reach_indeterminate 0. The other four zeros are a different family: current_capability 0, current_check_passed 0, gate_mutation 0, historical 0. The remaining ten reach keys are populated (reach_determined 43, observed_reach_holders 43, observed_reach_assets 43, reach_tvl_check 41, observed_reach_value_usd 38, observed_reach_unvalued_pairs/_assets/_reasons 5 each, observed_reach_priced_usd/_priced_holders 3 each). So B0b's 'the eight absent observed keys' reproduces exactly; the gap text's 'and 7 sibling observed keys' does not. WHY THE BRANCH NEVER FIRED — traced, and it is NOT unreachable code (not the L-16 shape) and NOT a producer defect: it is a three-conjunct data precondition. The floor is written at services/effects/recipes.py:1705-1707 inside `if not reach_holders:`, and _add_reach (:1545, called at :741) is reached only past the `if not value_moved and shape != SHAPE_CALLER_ARBITRARY: return emit(unknown(...))` gate at :703-735. So all three must hold: (1) a PROVEN fork value-out verdict exists — only 43 of the 87 protocol-1 flow.out claims have one; (2) value_holders non-empty (:1642 early return) — it is the PROTOCOL-WIDE holder set (services/effects/selection.py:1262-1266 folds _asset_holdings_by_deployment across every deployment), never empty on etherfi, so not the blocker; (3) ZERO (holder, asset) transfer-out pairs among the protocol's holdings. (3) is false on all 43: every proven row carries reason='value_moved' (43/43, and 0 rows carry 'caller_arbitrary_via_sentinel', the other path into _add_reach). The 5 reach_determined=false rows are ALL the unvalued-pairs branch at :1713 (they carry holders and reasons: BoringVault.exit x2, PriorityWithdrawalQueue.requestWithdrawWithWeETH, and two recoverETH rows), not the indeterminate branch. And the population the field was DESIGNED for never reaches the recipe: the 44 flow.out claims with no `observed` have NO effect_verdict_id whatsoever (tier idiom_structural 21, standard_exact 18, policy_derived 5); joining them to effect_verdicts on (address, selector, 'value_out') independently of the claim finds 30 unknown/reverted/'value_probe_reverted', 4 'timelock_holds_no_witness_asset', 3 'no_value_observed', 7 with no verdict row at all. The db/effect_cache.py v25 comment the gap cites is at :324-333 (not :328 exactly) and describes the fix correctly: the NUMBER did not change, the LABEL did — it moved off observed_reach_value_usd onto observed_reach_floor_usd + reach_determined=False + reach_indeterminate=True.

gaps.real: YES, and L-16 does NOT fully explain it — L-16 is SUPERSEDED. Verified: `select id, contract_address, witness->>'auto_expiry', witness->>'duration_bound_seconds', witness->>'duration_bound_source' from effect_verdicts where witness ? 'duration_bound_source'` -> exactly 4 rows (ids 137/149/173/219, all freeze_pause/proven/tier2, all selector 0x7e3db158 = pauseUntil(), all on RUNTIME proxy addresses), auto_expiry NULL 4/4, duration_bound_seconds NULL 4/4, duration_bound_source='not_determined' 4/4. On the claims plane the keys are present with jsonb-null values on 4/4. Vocabulary is at services/effects/config.py:131-133 (gap text correct); the consumer contract is claims_bridge.py:198-201 (correct). L-16 STATUS: the cited code (calldata.py:1823-1839, 'requires ONE guard leaf whose operand set holds all three') no longer exists — _duration_from_trees is now services/effects/calldata.py:2030-2160 and the harvest is _window_ceiling_constant at :1945-2027, which reads `absorbed_operands` (a widening added after L-16) and CAN recover a clock absorbed into arithmetic; db/effect_cache.py's v22 note records '10 of 11 compiled guard shapes went from None to the declared constant'. Two docstring claims are STALE IN THIS REPLICA and I refute one: _absorption_recorded (:1913-1941) asserts 'every contract_materializations.predicate_trees row in the database is such a tree [marker ABSENT]' — I fetched all 97 predicate_trees blobs from MinIO and ALL 1,503 trees carry `operand_absorption` set, with 117 leaves carrying absorbed_operands. So the 'no marker' explanation for the zero is FALSE here. THE ACTUAL BLOCKER is a NEW reachability limit beyond L-16: I ran _window_ceiling_constant over every leaf of all 97 materializations with a maximally generous hypothetical latch set (every state_variable_name appearing in any operand) -> 0 hits. Of the 21 absorbed leaves whose absorbed group holds a seconds clock, every one expresses the ceiling as a NAMED constant recorded as source='state_variable' with constant_value=None (MAX_FUTURE_LENGTH, MAX_RETROACTIVE_LENGTH, shareLockUpPeriodAtTimeOfDeposit), and _parse_int(operand.get('constant_value')) returns None for all of them — so the positive branch cannot fire on the mainstream Solidity idiom where the window is a named constant. INDEPENDENTLY, for THESE 4 rows the not_determined is the CORRECT, DOCUMENTED answer: calldata.py:2049-2059 states that etherfi's PausableUntil holds the window in storage ($.pauseUntilDuration) so saw_timed_latch_guard returns (None, not_determined) by design. auto_expiry is None purely BECAUSE of that: services/effects/anvil.py:250-262 gates the warp on `if max_pause_duration is not None and observed_blast:`. Confirmed on the wire side: across all 78 tier2 transcript blobs, max_pause_duration is None on 75/75, duration_bound_source='not_determined' on 75/75, auto_expiry None on 48/48 — nothing is measured and then dropped at projection. THE DECISIVE NEW MEASUREMENT: at pinned ethereum block 25643300 all four contracts answer nullary uint256 getters — pauseUntilDuration() = 172800 / 86400 / 28800 / 28800 (THREE distinct values across 4 rows, so it discriminates under inv.16), MAX_PAUSE_DURATION() = 2592000 on 4/4, MIN_PAUSE_DURATION() = 28800 on 4/4, pausedUntil() = 0 on 4/4. The freezes are 8h-2d auto-expiring, not indefinite, and the fact is readable.
gaps.fixable: The gating value enters at services/effects/orchestrator.py:517 (duration_bound_source=spec.duration_bound_source) and via the max_pause_duration parameter of pause_recipe (services/effects/anvil.py:163-187, consumed at :250-262); it is produced at services/effects/calldata.py:2604 (`duration, duration_source = read_max_pause_duration(facts, latch_vars)`) and :2612. Is the fact in scope? The AST/static side does NOT have it (the window is in storage, and the named-constant case has constant_value=None). The FORK side does: `transport` at anvil.py:250 can both read the contract and warp time, and the runtime address is already `contract_address` (anvil.py:184). So the fact is obtainable at the write point, but only by adding a read or a warp — not from anything already in scope.
gaps.provable: TWO CANDIDATES, one strictly stronger. (a) DETERMINISTIC ON-CHAIN READ (pinned block) of the declared ceiling: eth_call MAX_PAUSE_DURATION() at hex(block) on the runtime address, fed to the warp — anvil.py:253-257 already documents that over-warping past the declared maximum is sound ('a latch that has NOT expired by then is genuinely indefinite'). This is a selector match plus a duck type, so under inv.2 it needs the PR#161 negative control (a nonsense selector must revert) exactly as the getMinDelay classifier does; a catch-all fallback answering 2592000 would otherwise mint a bound from a name. Provable WITH that control; not provable without it. (b) STRICTLY PROVABLE AND NAME-FREE — a fork warp ladder: once the pause is observed effective with a non-empty blast radius, warp by an increasing ladder (+1s, +8h, +1d, +2d, +7d, +30d) re-running _succeeding_set at each rung; the smallest warp at which the ENTIRE observed blast radius succeeds again is a fork-OBSERVED upper bound on the freeze window, and an exhausted ladder is a fork-observed lower bound on indefiniteness. Reads no name, needs no constant and no AST fact — the same class of witness as pause_effective and latch_flip, already trusted on these 4 rows. NOT PROVABLE: deriving the window from the constant's NAME, from MIN_PAUSE_DURATION as a default, or concluding 'bounded' from the mere existence of a pauseUntilDuration() getter without a negative control. Also NOT provable as written: reading MAX_PAUSE_DURATION as a ceiling on the ACTUAL freeze requires that every write to the duration state be bounded by it — an AST claim over the write surface (the B5-limit-4 shape: enumerate the writers, then check each guard), derivable in principle from the predicate trees but a second, separate piece of work.
gaps.proposed_witness: Prefer (b): auto_expiry becomes a fork proof, plus new `expiry_observed_within_seconds` (the rung at which recovery was observed) and `expiry_ladder_exhausted_seconds` (the largest warp tried with no recovery). Publish duration_bound_source='fork_observed_recovery' as a FOURTH vocabulary value beside the three at services/effects/config.py:131-133. Optionally ALSO carry (a) as corroboration with its own provenance (`declared_ceiling_seconds`, `declared_ceiling_negative_control` in {passed, failed, not_established}) — two independent planes, never one laundered as two (cf. the anvil_version/foundry_version fabricated-corroboration trap).
gaps.honest_publication: If neither is built: duration_bound_source stays not_determined and duration contributes ZERO to severity in both directions, exactly as B0b/R12 requires and as B0b explicitly WITHDREW duration_bound_source as a citable inv.16b discriminator. In particular the inspector's current rendering of these latches as 'indefinite latch (no self-recovery bound)' — which calldata.py:2056-2059 names as a live defect about a latch literally called pauseUntil — is a not_determined published as a proven positive and must become 'window not determined' whether or not the fix lands. Note the asymmetry: because a shorter window LOWERS severity, an unproven bound must never be published; the ladder is admissible precisely because a recovery observation is a proof and not an assumption.
